introduction: Today we celebrate the Exaltation of the Holy Cross. In the desert, those bitten by serpents looked at the bronze serpent Moses raised and lived. Jesus says that the Son of Man must be lifted up in the same way, so that all who believe may have eternal life. Paul sings of Christ who humbled himself to death on a cross and was exalted by the Father. Let us adore the cross, the sign of God's love.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God so loved the world that he gave his only Son. Let us bring our prayers to him, who saves us through the cross.
intentions: For the Church: that she may glory in the cross of Christ and proclaim his saving love to all. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the Christians of the Holy Land and of the Middle East: that they may live in peace and freedom. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who suffer, in body or in spirit: that they may look to the cross and find life and hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who do not know God's love: that they may come to believe that God sent his Son to save, not to condemn. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may make the sign of the cross with faith and carry our crosses with love. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, you willed that your Son should save the world by the cross. Help us to know the mystery of his love on earth, and to share his glory in heaven. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Lifted up
reflection.body:
This feast goes back to the fourth century, to the dedication of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem, built over the place of Christ's death and Resurrection. On this day the Church lifts up the cross before the world, not as a sign of defeat but as a sign of victory and love.

The first reading tells a strange story. In the desert, the people complain against God, and poisonous snakes bite them. When they repent, God tells Moses: "Make a venomous snake, and set it on a pole. It shall happen that everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live." The very thing that brought death becomes, when lifted up, a sign of healing.

Jesus uses this image to speak of his own death: "As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life." On the cross, Jesus takes on himself the sin that wounds us, and those who look to him in faith are healed.

Then comes the reason: "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son." And the purpose: "For God didn't send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him."

Paul's hymn describes the whole movement: Christ "humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, yes, the death of the cross. Therefore God also highly exalted him."

The cross is on our walls, around our necks and in our churches. Today, look at a crucifix slowly and let it speak to you of God's love. Make the sign of the cross with care and faith, and offer God whatever wound you need him to heal.
